cards.text: Last time, Job lost his flocks, his herds, his servants and his children, and he still didn't sin (Job 1:13-22). Now, on another day, the sons of God come to present themselves before the LORD. And Satan, who came with them last time too, shows up AGAIN.

cards.question: The LORD asks Satan, "Where have you come from?" What does Satan say?

answers.text: From down by the Jordan River

cards.text: Then the LORD asks Satan, "Have you considered My servant Job?" He says there's no one on earth like him, blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil.

cards.question: After everything Job lost, the LORD tells Satan that Job still retains his ___.

cards.text: The LORD also says Satan incited Him against Job "to ruin him without cause." Satan is NOT letting this go, and he fires right back: "Skin for skin!"

cards.question: Satan says a man will give up all he owns in exchange for his life. So what does Satan ask the LORD to strike this time?
Satan claims that if Job's flesh and bones are struck, Job will surely curse God to His face.
The LORD agrees and puts Job in Satan's hands, with one limit. Satan must spare Job's ___.

cards.text: Satan goes out from the presence of the LORD and infects Job with terrible boils, from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head. Friend, I spent years in a dusty junk drawer thinking I had it rough, and I take it ALL back.

cards.question: Job sits among the ashes and takes a piece of broken ___ to scrape himself.

cards.text: Then Job's wife asks him, "Do you still retain your integrity?" There's that word again, the same one the LORD used about Job.

cards.question: What does Job's wife tell him to do?

cards.text: "You speak as a foolish woman speaks," Job tells her. Then he asks her a question of his own.

cards.question: Job asks his wife, "Should we accept from God only good and not ___?"
Covered in boils, Job finally sins in what he says.

cards.text: Now Job's three friends hear about all of it: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite. Each one leaves home and they meet up together, which is a group chat that actually DID something.

cards.question: Why do Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar come to see Job?

answers.text: To sympathize with him and comfort him
To help him rebuild his flocks and herds
To bring him back to live in their homes

cards.text: The three friends are still far off when they lift up their eyes and see Job.

cards.question: Even from far away, Job's three friends recognize him right away.
What do Job's three friends do when they see him like this?

answers.text: Weep aloud and tear their robes
Turn around and go back home
Call out to Job by his name

cards.question: Job's three friends sit on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights.
In all that time, no one says a word to Job. Why not?

answers.text: They see how intense his suffering is
They are too angry with Job to speak
They are waiting on a word from God

cards.text: Seven days without a word. Friend, I can't go seven MINUTES without talking, and trust me, this story is far from over.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "Should we accept from God only good and not ___?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question says 'After everything Job lost,' and card 1 already listed his children, flocks and herds as lost. That wording rules out the wrong answers 'fortune' and 'family' before the baker even thinks about it, so the card no longer tests anything.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a wording detail (broken pottery vs glass vs wood). Nothing earlier lets them reason it out, so the card tests unseen wording, not meaning. Ask about something the baker can reason from the scene, or tell the pottery on a story card.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Stop 1's story cards (1, 3, 5) read as plain narration with no real laugh. Papa Dorin's humor doesn't show up until stop 2. Moments like Satan showing up again or 'Skin for skin!' could carry a joke without muddying a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
